passage:
At the Sri Rama Navami fair in Chaitanya's village, Lalit anna played the harmonium on the temple steps, fingers flying, and the whole crowd clapped along. Chaitanya, nine, forgot all about his cotton candy.
On the walk home he announced to Ammamma, "From tomorrow I will practise harmonium every single day. Like Lalit anna!"
Ammamma's old harmonium sat under a cloth in the storeroom. Next morning Chaitanya dragged it out before brushing his teeth and pumped the bellows till dust flew. He played the same three notes over and over, grinning. After school he played again. After dinner he played on the veranda until the neighbour's dog howled.
"Every day," he told Ammamma, tapping her arm. "You'll see."

qa.q: Where did Lalit anna play the harmonium?
qa.a: On the temple steps at the Sri Rama Navami fair.

qa.q: What made Chaitanya want to practise every day?
qa.a: He admired Lalit anna and was thrilled by the clapping crowd, so excitement made him want to play like him.

qa.q: How could Ammamma help this excitement turn into a lasting habit?
qa.a: She could help Chaitanya choose a short, fixed practice time, so a routine is ready for the days when the thrill wears off.

qa.q: How might Ammamma feel hearing the same three notes all day?
qa.a: Ammamma may be amused and touched to hear her old harmonium played again, while wondering how long the excitement will last.

grounding: Shows a child in a village who admires a harmonium player at a fair and eagerly announces daily practice, carried along by excitement.

passage:
On Saturday, Jana's cousin Camila visited from Lisbon and drew everyone around the kitchen table in Berlin: Oma in her reading glasses, Papa mid-yawn, even the cat. The drawings looked alive. Jana, ten, couldn't stop staring at the moving pencil.
That night she found an empty notebook and wrote on the first page in big letters: JANA'S DRAWING BOOK. ONE DRAWING EVERY DAY.
On Sunday she drew her shoe, her lamp and the view from her window. On Monday she drew on the bus to school and again after homework.
"Look, Mama, I've done six already!" she said, holding up the book with smudgy grey fingers.
Mama smiled. "Every day, hm?"
"Every single day, like Camila," Jana said, already sharpening the pencil.

qa.q: What did Jana write on the first page of her notebook?
qa.a: JANA'S DRAWING BOOK. ONE DRAWING EVERY DAY.

qa.q: What does Jana's 'I've done six already!' show about how she feels?
qa.a: It shows she is proud and excited, eager to draw like Camila.

qa.q: What could Mama do to help the habit last once the excitement fades?
qa.a: Mama could help Jana pick a small daily drawing time and keep the book somewhere easy to reach, so it is simple to continue on duller days.

qa.q: How might Camila feel on hearing that Jana draws every day because of the visit?
qa.a: Camila might feel flattered and happy to have inspired Jana 😊, and could encourage her by drawing together next time.

grounding: Illustrates a child starting a daily drawing habit after admiring a cousin's sketches, with excitement making the new habit feel easy.

passage:
Looking back, it started at my cousin Pradeep's match. He hit a six, and the whole ground cheered. I decided right then: I would practise cricket every single day.
The next morning I woke up before the alarm. I bowled against the wall for an hour. I told Mummy, "I'm going to be like Pradeep bhaiya." I told my class teacher. I told the watchman.
For the first week it was so easy. I didn't even need anyone to remind me. I just jumped out of bed, grabbed the ball, and ran.
I'm Parul, and that was my cricket week. My arm still remembers.

qa.q: Where did Parul see Pradeep hit a six?
qa.a: At Pradeep's match.

qa.q: What was Parul feeling after seeing the six?
qa.a: Parul felt excited and full of admiration for Pradeep bhaiya, wanting to be just like him.

qa.q: What could help Parul keep practising once the excitement fades?
qa.a: Choosing a set small time each day, like ten minutes after school, so practice doesn't depend on feeling excited.

qa.q: How might Pradeep feel if he heard about Parul's week?
qa.a: Pradeep would probably feel proud and flattered that his six inspired his young cousin.

grounding: Shows a child deciding to practise cricket every day after watching an admired cousin, finding it easy while excitement lasts.

passage:
Harmonium teacher's note, Saturday
Gurleen came to class today practically bouncing. Last weekend she heard an older student play at the gurdwara and announced, "I'm going to practise every single day, like her!" Her mother says she has practised every morning this week, before breakfast, without being asked.
Today she played her scales twice as long as usual and asked for a new song. Her eyes lit up when I played it for her.
I praised her effort. I also suggested we choose a fixed ten-minute slot, so practice becomes a habit that still happens on days she doesn't feel so excited. She wrote "10 min after school" on her book herself.
Jatin

qa.q: When has Gurleen been practising this week?
qa.a: Every morning, before breakfast.

qa.q: What was Gurleen feeling when she came to class?
qa.a: She felt excited and inspired, full of admiration for the older student she heard.

qa.q: Why did Jatin suggest a fixed ten-minute slot?
qa.a: So practice becomes a habit that still happens when the excitement fades.

qa.q: How might Gurleen's mother feel watching her practise every morning?
qa.a: She is probably pleased and a little amused at how eager Gurleen is.

grounding: Shows a teacher's note on a child who, after hearing an admired older student, starts practising daily with easy excitement.

passage:
Dear Diary,
Today Ojas bhaiya from the third floor showed me his drawings. He draws cars that look REAL. I want to draw like that.
So I decided. I will draw every day. Every single day! I drew three cars today, one before school, one at lunch, and one now. The wheels were wobbly but I don't care.
I asked Mumma to buy a new sketchbook and she said yes. I am going to fill it by the end of the month.
I'm so excited I can't sleep. Tomorrow I will draw a truck.
Raghav

qa.q: How many cars did Raghav draw today?
qa.a: Three cars.

qa.q: What is Raghav feeling as he goes to bed?
qa.a: Raghav feels excited and inspired by admiration for Ojas bhaiya's drawings, too excited to sleep.

qa.q: What small plan could help Raghav keep drawing after the excitement fades?
qa.a: Picking one fixed time each day, such as ten minutes after dinner, and keeping it even on dull days.

qa.q: How might Ojas feel knowing Raghav wants to draw like him?
qa.a: Ojas would probably feel flattered and proud to have inspired a younger neighbour.

grounding: Shows a child deciding to draw every day after admiring a neighbour's work, finding it easy while the excitement lasts.

passage: At the Ram Navami bhajan in the village temple, a girl only a few years older than Anjali played the harmonium so fast her fingers blurred, and the whole courtyard clapped along. Walking home under the neem trees, Anjali could not stop talking. "Indu Bua, I'm going to play harmonium every single day. Every day! Even Sundays. Even when it rains." At home she pulled Dadi's old harmonium out from under the cot, blew off the dust and pumped the bellows until it wheezed. She pressed the same three keys for an hour, grinning, and drew a chart with thirty boxes on the back of a calendar page. Indu Bua smiled. "Let's see how the boxes look after the mela is over."

qa.q: How many boxes did Anjali draw on her chart?
qa.a: Thirty boxes, on the back of a calendar page.

qa.q: What feeling was driving Anjali's big promise?
qa.a: She was excited and inspired after watching the older girl play so fast, and wanted to play like her.

qa.q: What could help Anjali keep going once the excitement fades?
qa.a: A small, fixed practice time and someone to play for now and then, so it does not depend on excitement alone.

qa.q: Why might Indu Bua smile at the promise?
qa.a: Indu Bua enjoys Anjali's excitement but hints, with the remark about the mela, that the promise will be harder to keep later.

grounding: Shows a child announcing a daily practice plan right after watching someone admired, driven by excitement that makes starting easy.
